audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing in either layer mentions that Maokai is untargetable during Twisted Advance. The advice given is the opposite of usable: content.mid says 'Hold Wither for the moment he commits a W-root' and content.wants.you[1] says 'Hold Wither for his W-root engage'.
audit.why: Riot's text: 'Maokai contorts into a mass of moving roots, BECOMING UNTARGETABLE and dashing to the target.' Wither is a targeted cast. A Nasus who holds Wither for the moment Maokai commits the W will click and get nothing, then be rooted with his one defensive cooldown still in hand and no time to use it. The correct instruction is to Wither before he casts, or the instant he arrives — never during.
audit.corrected: He is untargetable for the whole Twisted Advance dash. Wither lands before he casts or after he arrives, never in between.
sources: champ-data/_kits/maokai.json W description and untargetable flag

audit.whatIsWrong: full.breakdown.cooldowns contradicts itself inside one string: '- Maokai Twisted Advance (Root): matchup-defining — His lock-on root. Dodge it.' followed immediately by '- Maokai Twisted Advance: Dashes to a target and roots them — lock-on, undodgeable. Dodge or sidestep it.' The same ability is listed twice, once as dodgeable and once as undodgeable. full.dosFull[0].d and dosFull[2].t repeat the 'dodge it' instruction.
audit.why: It is lock-on, so it cannot be sidestepped. Telling a player to dodge an undodgeable ability wastes the only real counterplay, which is baiting the cast or being outside its 525 range.
audit.corrected: Twisted Advance is lock-on and cannot be dodged — bait it or stay outside 525.

audit.whatIsWrong: Maokai's healing is attributed to his saplings throughout — 'his passive sustain', 'his passive saplings can heal it back', 'Sustain through your Spirit Fire with passive saplings'. Saplings are Sapling Toss (E) and they do not heal him.
audit.why: The heal is Sap Magic (P), which fires on a basic attack. Crucially its cooldown is reduced every time Maokai casts a spell OR is struck by an enemy's spell. That inverts the usual read: chipping a Maokai with spell damage shortens the timer on his own healing. A Nasus poking with Spirit Fire and wondering why the tank never drops is being punished by a mechanic nothing in this file names.
audit.corrected: Sap Magic (P) is the heal, on a basic attack. Every spell he casts or eats brings it back sooner.

audit.whatIsWrong: No Grievous Wounds guidance anywhere, despite Sap Magic being the reason the file says his sustain 'answers your poke'.
audit.why: The matchup is a scaling grind that Nasus is meant to win by out-damaging a tank's regeneration. Anti-heal is the item decision that settles it, and it is flagged for this exact matchup in _missing-interactions.
audit.corrected: Buy Grievous Wounds — Sap Magic is what keeps his HP bar ahead of your empowered Q.

audit.whatIsWrong: The packet flags 'NO cooldown-sequencing advice anywhere', and breakdown.cooldowns supplies two entries for the same ability with no numbers on either.
audit.why: The real numbers make the lane legible: Sapling Toss is 18/17/16/15/14s — by far his longest lane cooldown and the actual window to step up and stack — while Twisted Advance is 14/13/12/11/10s and Bramble Smash only 7/6.5/6/5.5/5s. Nature's Grasp at 130/110/90 is also slower than Nasus's own 120/100/80.
audit.corrected: Sapling Toss 18/17/16/15/14 is the window. Twisted Advance 14 to 10. Bramble Smash 7 to 5.

audit.why: content.late's claim that Maokai has no true damage and no percent-health is accurate — neither flag appears anywhere in his kit. I left it because in this matchup it is the load-bearing reason Nasus's health bar actually functions as a win condition, not filler.
49.83% over 291 games — a genuine coinflip, and the chart (Maokai levels 2-5, even at 6 and first item, Nasus late) reflects that honestly.

edits.before: Maokai owns the first few levels here — his saplings chip you while you're trying to last-hit with Siphoning Strike, and his W-root dash into Q-knockback punishes any greedy step-up before you have Wither. Don't trade autos into him; just soak Q farm and let Soul Eater lifesteal heal the sapling poke. You have no ult and barely any stacks, so there's nothing to win — eat the lane and stack.
edits.after: Maokai owns the first few levels — Sapling Toss (E) chips you while you last-hit with Siphoning Strike, and Twisted Advance (W) into Bramble Smash (Q) punishes any greedy step-up before you have Wither. He is untargetable during the W dash, so Wither cannot land on it. Don't trade autos into him; soak Q farm and let Soul Eater lifesteal heal the sapling poke.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 stay his — he shoves with saplings and roots you out of Spirit Fire, and his passive sustain answers your poke. Hold Wither for the moment he commits a W-root, because slowing his attack speed and movement turns his all-in into a free reset. At 6, Fury of the Sands plus Wither lets you survive or flip a single committed engage, so stop conceding and start contesting the wave.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 stay his — Sapling Toss shoves and Twisted Advance roots you out of Spirit Fire, and Sap Magic (P) heals it back. Sap Magic returns faster every time he casts a spell or eats one, so spell poke feeds his sustain; buy Grievous Wounds. Hold Wither for the instant he LANDS a W, never the dash — he is untargetable in flight. At 6 Fury of the Sands plus Wither flips one committed engage.

notes: The packet's suspectName ('Spirit Fire's' in spikes[3].text) is a FALSE POSITIVE — correct name plus possessive. Both other flagged defects were real. The untargetability on Twisted Advance is the important find: the file's stated Wither timing does not work against it, and that is a mistake a player only discovers by losing the fight. The Sap Magic cooldown-refresh mechanic is the second: it means poking a Maokai with spells partly heals him, which flips the intuitive read of the lane. I stated the refresh exactly as Riot words it ('every spell he casts or eats') and deliberately did not claim anything about whether Spirit Fire's individual damage ticks each count as being struck by a spell — that is a wiki question I could not settle from the kit file, and it materially changes how bad Spirit Fire poke is here. Worth verifying.
